summary:
The fixed execution decided the question in the direction the local run predicted, and the interpretation, its fact, and a control-scoping successor are recorded in one file (valid:true).

Verified defect — `GetConfiguration().Index()` does not identify the returned configuration, and the documented optimistic-concurrency guard cannot be expressed with it (receipt 5466e7c2853749f6849e40362a2cdf00, completed/exit 0). Comparison 0 came back violated: indices 4, 5 and 7 (leader, server-22ab50bc, server-ee231480) report returned_index 0 with returned_servers 4 and the reference configuration entry index 3, each matched to its own config_guard_start admission; index 6 is correctly outside applicability because that node still showed three servers at read time. Comparison 1 also violated: after an intervening change (index 8, entry 4) the change guarded with the value the API returned succeeded with rpc_error empty and entry 5 (index 9). The control operand at index 10 shows the contrast: guarded with the genuine index 3 the same change failed with "configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)". Source mechanism: GetConfiguration fills the returned future from the atomically published latest Configuration only (api.go:895-903), configurationsFuture.Index returns that zeroed field (future.go:255-270), and nextConfiguration enforces prevIndex only when it is greater than zero (configuration.go:228-231) against the documented prevIndex contract (api.go:941-957). Conclusion recorded as violated, scoped explicitly as a client-contract and concurrency-guard defect, not a consensus-safety defect; internal configuration tracking was not shown to be affected, and callers that pass prevIndex 0 keep their documented unconstrained behaviour. The investigation is closed as explained with those boundaries, including that the control comparison in this receipt was unknown because of my admission scoping, so the control rests on its retained operand.

A fact was promoted with the observed operands (indices 4, 5, 7, 9, 10), and a successor experiment is requested with previous_id and a documented revision reason: the harness (draft/assurance_getconfig_index_v2.go) adds a leader-scoped `leader_change_window_start` admission so both leader-side comparisons are decided instead of correlated against three nodes that never produce those results; producers, cluster shape and parameters are unchanged, and the local run of the fixed harness reproduced the same operand pattern.
